The task of cross-domain text-to-SQL parsing is challenging, particularly when faced with a lack of training data for a specific target domain. This problem is further complicated by the need to accurately identify the meaning of SQL queries, which involves both parsing and semantic analysis. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach that utilizes a supportive task, specifically a cross-domain text-to-SQL generation task, to facilitate the parsing process. This supportive task is designed to leverage the abundance of unstructured text data available across various domains, which can be easily converted into SQL code. By integrating the supportive task into the parsing process, we create a unified end-to-end framework that enables the model to learn from both unstructured text and SQL code across multiple domains. Experimental results on the Spider dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach, which outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin. Furthermore, our approach achieves comparable performance to existing methods when trained on a single domain, showcasing its adaptability. Additionally, we conduct an ablation study to validate the contribution of the supportive task and the proposed framework. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/chenxu1997/CT2SQL.

Experimental results show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on both tasks, and achieves a significant improvement in terms of coherence and relevance. Additionally, we conduct an ablation study to analyze the contribution of each component of our approach, and a human evaluation study to assess the quality of generated text.
